questions.q: What is DBFS, at a high level?
options: A filesystem abstraction letting you address cloud storage using ordinary-looking paths, rather than a separate physical disk
A brand-new physical storage device inside every Databricks cluster
A replacement for Delta Lake
A pricing tier for Azure Databricks workspaces
questions.explain: The actual bytes still live in whatever cloud storage account is backing it — DBFS is a convenience layer.

questions.q: What's the relationship between %fs and dbutils.fs?
options: %fs is the magic-command shortcut; dbutils.fs is the same functionality called directly from Python
They are unrelated features with no overlap
%fs only works in SQL cells, dbutils.fs only in R cells
dbutils.fs is deprecated in favor of %fs
questions.explain: dbutils.fs is useful anywhere a magic command wouldn't fit, like inside a function.

questions.q: What is a "mount" in the DBFS context?
options: A DBFS path pointing at a real, separate cloud storage container, like an ADLS Gen2 container from Foundations
A temporary in-memory cache that disappears when a cluster stops
A synonym for DBFS root with no real distinction
A feature only available with Unity Catalog volumes
questions.explain: That data can potentially be shared with other tools outside Databricks entirely.

questions.q: Why does Databricks now steer production data away from DBFS root?
options: DBFS root has no Unity Catalog governance attached to it at all — a Unity Catalog volume is the current recommended path instead
DBFS root is being fully removed from Databricks with no replacement
DBFS root only supports read operations, never writes
DBFS root is significantly slower than every other storage option
questions.explain: A Unity Catalog volume (Lesson 45) offers the same addressable file storage idea, but with real access control.

questions.q: Is DBFS still worth knowing, given the shift toward Unity Catalog volumes?
options: Yes — it's the historical default and still used constantly for scratch/testing work, even as production data moves toward volumes
No, DBFS has been completely removed from Databricks
Only if a workspace doesn't have Unity Catalog enabled
Only for reading data, never for writing it
questions.explain: Chapter 4 covers the volumes-based path real production pipelines should now take.
